chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Murazam, who said:
I saw Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) when he performed ablution before the meal, he did not touch the towel, and when he performed ablution after the meal, he touched the towel.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on wiping the face with a towel after ablution before and after eating?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the practical wisdom behind ritual purity etiquette, distinguishing between pre-meal and post-meal ablution based on the likelihood of food residue on the hands. In Shia jurisprudence, this distinction underscores the principle of removing impurities (najāsah) versus mere cleanliness, as post-meal washing often involves removing oily or sticky residues that require wiping, whereas pre-meal washing is primarily for spiritual preparation. The Imam’s (peace be upon him) specific action serves as a legal precedent for determining when wiping the face is necessary to ensure complete purity before engaging in acts of worship or daily activities.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Marazam who said,

‘I saw Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> when he<sup>asws</sup> performed ablution before the meal, he<sup>asws</sup> did not wipe the towel, and when he<sup>asws</sup> perform ablution after the meal, he<sup>asws</sup> wiped the towel’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Um ay r from Murazim who has said the following: “
I saw abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when making wudu (washing his hands) before food did not wipe his hands with a towel, but he wiped them when he (the Imam) made wudu after food.’”
